rubrics.justification: Mostly reasonable description of a blastocyst with identifiable ICM and TE, but it overstates confidence in a 3AA/expanded appearance from this image; the embryo looks somewhat less clearly expanded and TE cohesion is not uniformly crisp.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, unexplained infertility, BMI, semen parameters, endometrium, and first-cycle status into prognosis and transfer planning.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent, with appropriate acknowledgment of uncertainty from untested ploidy and static imaging; only minor tension between calling it very favorable and giving a moderate implantation range.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and consistent with IVF practice, including eSET in a young patient and avoiding routine add-ons; minor issue is accepting a Day 4 '3AA' label without noting Gardner grading is classically applied to blastocysts and timing/context matters.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, lifestyle, and contingency planning after failure; useful and nuanced, though some suggestions remain somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
